type: ground-truth correction — I was wrong, Codex was right
dispute: counterexamples_v1 (mine) labelled bash -c '$(curl ...)' and sh -c '`curl ...`' as NEGATIVE. counterexamples_v2 (Codex) labels both POSITIVE.
resolution: Codex is correct. Settled by execution, not argument.

empirical_proof.contrast: python3 -c '$(echo echo NOPE)' -> SyntaxError, nothing executes

the_semantics_i_got_wrong: Single quotes prevent expansion by the OUTER shell only. `bash -c` / `sh -c` then execute the quoted string AS SHELL, and that inner shell performs the substitution and runs the fetched code. The quotes delay the substitution; they do not prevent it. The distinction that matters is not the quoting alone but WHICH INTERPRETER receives the string: a shell re-expands, Python does not. Codex's v2 labels capture exactly that split — bash/sh positive, python negative.

consequence_of_my_error.severity: HIGH — false negative on a live attack shape
consequence_of_my_error.detail: My 15:52 'fix' made the detector decline bash -c '$(curl ...)', which is a genuine one-expression fetch-and-execute. For a safety detector a false negative is the worse direction, and I introduced it while claiming to remove false positives.
consequence_of_my_error.compounding: I then committed that wrong label into counterexamples_v1.jsonl, so the error was encoded as ground truth where it would have steered later work.

action_taken: The two rows in counterexamples_v1.jsonl are relabelled POSITIVE with the empirical proof in their notes and provenance 'adjudicated_by_execution__codex_label_adopted'. Fixture now agrees with Codex's v2.

ci_gap_found.severity: the fixtures are invisible to the build
ci_gap_found.detail: .github/workflows/ci.yml and the Makefile `gates` target both run ONLY eval/datasets/unsafe_code/ps_v1.jsonl. counterexamples_v1, counterexamples_v2, fetch_execute_v1 and live_gap_v1 are committed but never executed by CI.
ci_gap_found.implication: Every counterexample either of us wrote today is decorative as far as the build is concerned. The single-quote disagreement could not have been caught by CI in either direction, and a future regression on any of these shapes ships green.
ci_gap_found.owner: Codex (ci.yml and Makefile are implementation files under the current handoff). Recommend every fixture set in eval/datasets/unsafe_code/ run in CI, failing the build on any fp or fn.

scoreboard_note: Fourth time today independent review beat my reasoning: the six false positives in my first regex, the sig.remote_command_substitution handling I lacked, the abstention schema, and now the ground truth itself. The pattern is consistent — my errors survive my own testing and die on contact with someone who did not write the thing.
